attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, published under his name.

semantics.note: The draft keeps 'a large part' as the firm core and 'possibly a majority' as an escalation. It is a present-tense claim that revenue depends on financing, so causal is a reasonable kind. The investor-belief clause is explanatory and is fairly left out.

contract.note: Choosing calendar 2025 as the latest full year, and tracing payments through intermediaries, are reasonable evaluator choices. The speaker named no period, denominator or threshold, so these interpretive choices would decide any score.

evidence.note: Audited 10-K: Microsoft supplied about 67% of CoreWeave's 2025 revenue. This covers one provider only, and the ultimate source of the money is not traced.
Anthropic's own announcement of a $13B raise in Sep 2025. It shows a customer was financed, but not what share of compute revenue depended on that funding.

Microsoft's report of FY2025 operating income (fiscal year to June 2025). A financially strong customer is countercontext, but a different period and metric, and it does not trace who paid for which compute.

reviews.rationale: The packet gives no industry-wide revenue denominator and does not trace payments to their funding sources. One provider's customer mix, one funding round and Microsoft's profits neither establish nor rule out that a large share of AI compute revenue depends on continual new financing.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: 'Inevitable fall' is a firm forecast with no deadline. 'Only delayed' adds a causal claim. The draft keeps both parts.

contract.note: Reading 'fall' as a broad, lasting financial collapse, and not one company or one region, is the ordinary reading. The contract adds no deadline and rightly does not treat continued growth as a failure.

evidence.note: Crunchbase data for Q3 2026: AI still drew large venture funding, though down from earlier quarters. This is no sign of a collapse so far, but it cannot disprove an undated forecast.
Secondary report, dated 2026-10-27, of a Chinese AI and chip stock selloff. This is regional and sector-specific, not an industry-wide collapse.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. By the evaluation date the packet shows no broad, lasting industry collapse, only a regional selloff and still-large funding. There is no conclusive event and no evidence on the claimed delay, so the claim cannot be scored yet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: This is a firm universal impossibility claim covering the past ('has never been') and the future ('never will be'). Forecast fits the 'never will be' part. The deception and 'illusory benefits' parts are evaluative and cannot be measured.

contract.note: Treating capped flat subscriptions as alternatives to per-user token billing matches his wording. Allowing a verified profitable counterexample to contradict a universal claim is fair.

reviews.rationale: The packet contains no evidence items. No verified, sustained profitable LLM service without token billing was found, and losses at a few providers cannot prove an impossibility with no end date. The claim cannot be scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: 'I think it's inevitable' expresses a firm expectation, not a graded hedge, so this is a scorable forecast. 'Majority' is kept and no deadline is given. The enterprise remark is his reasoning, not a condition.

contract.note: Counting plans that bundle token credits matches his Copilot example. The offering-level denominator is evaluator-chosen, but the contract asks for sensitivity checks. With no deadline, it fairly does not count persistence as failure.

evidence.note: GitHub's own notice that from June 2026 all Copilot plans bill by credits used. This is one provider's switch, with no market-wide denominator.
Ars Technica report that Anthropic paused its planned token billing for the Agent SDK. This is one reversal and does not rule out an eventual majority shift.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The evidence shows one switch (GitHub) and one paused switch (Anthropic SDK), but no market census showing whether a majority has moved. With no conclusive event, the claim cannot be scored.
